import pandas as pd


DESCRIPTION = "RSI mean reversion: long while the 14-day RSI is below 40 (oversold)."

N_TRIALS = 1
PARAM_GRID = None


def run(prices: pd.DataFrame, period: int = 14, entry: float = 40.0) -> pd.Series:
    c = prices["close"]
    delta = c.diff()
    gain = delta.clip(lower=0).rolling(period).mean()
    loss = (-delta.clip(upper=0)).rolling(period).mean()
    rsi = 100 - 100 / (1 + gain / loss)
    signal = (rsi < entry).astype(float)
    return signal.shift(1).fillna(0.0)

plan.strategy_summary: The strategy goes long when the 14‑day RSI falls below 40, indicating oversold conditions, and exits otherwise.

test_plan.hypothesis: Shifting the signal by one bar removes any same‑bar lookahead, so performance should remain stable.
Positions depend only on data up to the prior bar, so truncating the series and adjusting the last close will not alter earlier signals.
No parameter grid is defined, thus the walk‑forward test is not applicable.
On a random walk the deflated Sharpe will warn due to chance fluctuations, which is expected even for an honest strategy.

tests.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 bar barely changed results (Sharpe -0.43 -> -0.27).
Positions were identical with the future hidden on all 40 dates checked.
No parameter search declared, so there's nothing to walk forward.
Confidence the edge is real is 9% (below 95%): results aren't statistically significant yet.

report.headline: No evidence of lookahead, leakage, or overfitting was found; the strategy’s edge is not statistically proven.

tests.explanation: Delaying the signal by one bar barely changed results (Sharpe moved from -0.43 to -0.27), showing no same‑bar lookahead.
Positions were identical when future data was hidden on all 40 dates checked, confirming the strategy uses only past information.
No parameter grid was defined, so there is nothing to walk forward over.
Confidence the edge is real is 9% (below 95%), meaning the result is not statistically significant given the single trial.

report.caveats: The audit was run on synthetic or random data; a WARN verdict means the edge is not proven, not that the strategy is definitely flawed. Results may differ on real market data.
